ctx.x: This is what I want -- I'm going to interrupt you, Crook. Without doubt, your voice -- you're one of the finest voices and vocalists that I've ever heard and we've worked together now for 12 years or more but the most amazing thing to me is your memory of lyrics. You might not remember the name of the room we're playing in, you might not remember the title of a song but once you hear it, once you hear the opening bars, you've got the lyrics.

I can remember so well one night in Chicago when we were featuring a trombone player there and a wonderful trombone player, Jim Bibe; remember he joined the band for that engagement, and his classic solo was "Blue Prelude". Now we had never done that on my band and when your chorus

came for the guitar, you sang it and you didn't miss a word and I've seen you do this over and over again. We get requests for numbers that we've never played together that you hadn't played or heard for 30 years but you remember the lyrics and I think it's one of the most amazing things, very seriously. I've never seen anybody do this. I've never even heard of anybody doing it. What is the secret of remembering lyrics of numbers you haven't heard for 30 years?
